_: THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN context budget -- the canonical methodology repo dogfooding starter-kit/context_budget.py on itself. Provisioned from starter-kit/context-budget.json (the SEED adopters receive) and then calibrated to THIS tree at cea3068 (read-set-budgets after PR #78). Every ceiling below states its derivation in the neighbouring _ key; numbers marked PROPOSAL are the fork's choices offered to the maintainer, not measurements. THE TOOL IS NOT AT THIS REPO'S ROOT: bin/_manifest.py installs it at ADOPTER roots; canonically it lives only at starter-kit/context_budget.py. Invoke it as `python3 starter-kit/context_budget.py` -- find_root() walks up via .git and reads this file. DO NOT RUN `install-hook` HERE. On a fresh clone core.hooksPath is unset, so install-hook WRITES .git/hooks/pre-commit exec'ing <root>/context_budget.py, which does not exist at this root, and every commit after that fails with `can't open file`; recover with `rm .git/hooks/pre-commit`. With `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` set (BOOTSTRAP Step 10) it declines instead, because that hook is the FM #27 ledger gate. The budget gate therefore MEASURES here: run `python3 starter-kit/context_budget.py --precommit` by hand before a commit that touches a budgeted file, or chain it into .githooks/pre-commit as a separate, deliberate change. Refusing to run without this file (exit 3, `refuses to invent budgets`) is the tool's own 1.0.0 behaviour, unchanged by the 1.2.0 port.
_precommit_scope: `--precommit` sizes the INDEX against HEAD for each declared file and class; it evaluates NEITHER the `structure` patterns NOR `max_lines` below. Those run in the bare and --json modes only, where a pattern that stops matching reports `instrument-failed`. Bare and --json runs CREATE .context-budget-history.jsonl on the first run and append to it only when the measurement changes (the file reappears on every later run); --precommit, --selftest, --calibrate and --help write nothing.
_read_cap_tokens: The per-read cap in TOKENS: the number in the Claude Code Read tool's own refusal message (`File content (N tokens) exceeds maximum allowed tokens (25000)`), first observed 2026-08-26 and re-confirmed 2026-09-03 on Claude Code 2.1.259 (`claude --version`). Reproduce it in one action: Read any file larger than the cap with an explicit `limit` that spans it -- the tool returns no content and prints that message, whose parenthesised number is this key's value; a Read without a limit returns a partial view whose banner names the same cap. The tool's module default READ_CAP_TOKENS carries the same value, so this key restates the default rather than changing it; the seed edit in this same PR declares it for adopters. It is a fact about the harness, not a policy: if yours differs, set this key and every derived ceiling below follows.
_bytes_per_token: INHERITED FROM THE SEED, NOT MEASURED ON THIS REPO. It is the fallback density for any file below that declares none of its own -- on this config that is NO file since S22 (CLAUDE.md carries its measured 2.519); kept for any future entry that declares none (`--json` shows density_source config on such a file). The two read-set members carry per-file densities MEASURED on the blobs the merge into main produces (see their entries), and the Learnings table gets no token verdict. `python3 starter-kit/context_budget.py --calibrate` fits this repo's own value from its session transcripts; it PROPOSES and writes nothing -- edit this key if the fit is admitted (R^2 >= 0.50, positive slope).
_fixed_harness_tokens: INHERITED FROM THE SEED, NOT MEASURED ON THIS REPO, and READ BY NOTHING in context_budget.py 1.2.0 (grep it); carried for seed parity so a future consumer finds the seed's value. Same remedy if one appears: --calibrate.
_growth_run: INHERITED FROM THE SEED, NOT DERIVED. It cannot be calibrated on day one: this repo has no .context-budget-history.jsonl until this config's first bare run, so the series the trigger reads is empty. Decide whether to track that file once it exists (the fork tracks it, deliberately; see .gitignore).
_calibrate_against: The resident file --calibrate fits session tokens against, and the regressor the two TestFitGateEndToEnd tests use on a machine that has this checkout's transcripts. Running --calibrate and adopting or rejecting its fit is the maintainer's step after merge; the build session does not run it (it would skip in a clean clone -- no transcripts under the clone's slug).

resident._: Resident is a ONE-FILE class in this repo -- CLAUDE.md is the only artifact the harness injects in full before the session starts; there is no root SESSION_RUNNER.md (the runner is the distributed starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md) and no root SESSION_NOTES.md (continuity lives in HANDOFFS.md). So this total equals CLAUDE.md's own ceiling by construction. That is deliberate and it is NOT a check that cannot fail: the per-file ceiling cannot see a SECOND resident file being added, and this one can. Agent-level memory (~/.claude/projects/.../MEMORY.md) is genuinely resident too but is per-operator and per-machine, outside this repo, and not a reviewable diff -- deliberately excluded. PROPOSAL: PINNED AT ARRIVAL SIZE (git cat-file -s cea3068:CLAUDE.md = 59,168 B), a ratchet, not a defended budget: growth is refused, shrink passes. The seed's 34,000 B total would read `over` by 25,168 B on day one for a reason unrelated to the read-set work; the pin states the true size and leaves the target to the maintainer.

read-set._: THE PHASE 0 MANDATORY READ -- starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md, the procedure itself (`Follow it step by step`, its line 3; CLAUDE_TEMPLATE.md orders it read), plus starter-kit/SAFEGUARDS.md, which its step 1 orders read in full. DECLARED WITH NO CLASS CEILING, deliberately (PR #80 review F3). What is at stake is whether ONE Read delivers the pair, and the read cap is denominated in TOKENS; a class ceiling can only be written in BYTES -- class_ceiling() takes a typed total_bytes or derives one at the 2.27 B/token floor (derive_from_read_cap: 25,000 x 2.27 = 56,750 B), and the floor is for a file nobody can meter. This pair has been metered. So the cap is enforced per file, in tokens, at each file's measured density: the two max_tokens below, 18,900 + 6,100, partition the 25,000-token read cap exactly, so the pair cannot pass the cap unless a member passes its own ceiling; the class total is still reported, as a measurement, with no ceiling beside it. THE SUM IS HELD BY A TEST, not by prose: tools/test_context_budget.py TestThisRepoReadSetPartition fails any edit whose per-file ceilings in the read-set class exceed read_cap_tokens (PR #80 re-review G1 -- with the byte class ceiling gone, nothing mechanical held the partition; a 22,000 mutant reported OK). THE PAIR, MEASURED by the doubled-file method (concatenate the two files, double the result, Read it with a spanning `limit`, halve the token count the refusal reports): 23,902 tokens on this branch (67,581 B; the doubled read reports 47,805, the figure this PR's description records) and 24,278 on its merge into main at 9fa3141 (68,548 B; doubled 48,555), 97.1% of the cap. The 967 B between them is main's own S16 paragraph in SAFEGUARDS.md, not this branch. At the 2.27 floor the merged pair would count 30,197 tokens, which is why the floor-derived 56,750 B total this class used to declare read OVER on arrival. The byte-denominated class is recoverable with `git show 37740763:.context-budget.json`. If read_cap_tokens changes, re-partition the two max_tokens by hand: they are typed against 25,000 and do not follow it, and the partition test above is what makes a re-split safe. RE-SPLIT 2026-09-15 (S20) from 19,200 + 5,800: the quality-ratchet plan (D3) adds a Blast Radius row to SAFEGUARDS.md, and a pin at the file's exact size would have refused it; 300 tokens moved from the runner's margin to the safeguards file.

structure.why: Twelve links in this repo's CHANGELOG.md and one test fixture (tools/test_methodology_trim.py) resolve to CLAUDE.md#versioning on cea3068; a compaction that removes or renames the heading breaks them silently. (CLAUDE.md itself states no such rule here -- that sentence exists only in the fork's copy.) Evaluated by the bare run only, not by --precommit.

files._: TOKEN CEILING 23,483 AT A MEASURED DENSITY (S22, 2026-09-16, PR #82 review section 3): the byte pin could not see that the S20 reduction went the OTHER way in tokens -- 59,168 -> 59,153 B was 23,420.5 -> 23,482.5 tokens (doubled reads 46,841 and 46,965), because the new table rows are dense with backticked paths and the prose cut to pay for them was not. bytes_per_token 2.519 was 59,153 / 23,482.5, measured on blob 1244e95b. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-17 on blob dd416ea (59,119 B, after the action-ledger wording): the doubled read reports 46,953, so the file is 23,476.5 and bytes_per_token is 2.5182; the same run reproduced 1244e95b's 46,965. Re-measure when that blob changes. max_tokens 23,483 is a no-growth pin at the measured size (the tool counts int(59,153 / 2.519) = 23,482, 1 under; at dd416ea, int(59,119 / 2.5182) = 23,476); max_bytes 59,168 stays as the coarse backstop. At the seed's 2.93 fallback the tool reported 20,188 tokens and ~4,800 of headroom where there were ~1,500. max_lines 200 is THIS FRAMEWORK'S OWN PUBLISHED NUMBER, not an invention: starter-kit/BOOTSTRAP.md ('Keep CLAUDE.md lean') says Claude Code targets roughly 200 lines and tells adopters to extract before that budget is crowded. The file is 126 lines on cea3068 (the tool counts 127: it keeps the empty string after the final newline, but the check (context_budget.py:366) is a strict >, so 200 fires at wc -l 200, when the tool counts 201), so this arm is green on arrival. max_bytes is a PROPOSAL, PINNED AT ARRIVAL SIZE -- see classes.resident. NO warn_bytes: a warning threshold below a pin set at the current size would fire on every run and inform nobody. NO protected_fence, deliberately: the seed's budget:protected fence does not exist in this file, and declaring it would report `over` for a missing fence -- a red manufactured by this config rather than a real defect. Adding the fence is an edit to CLAUDE.md, raised separately. TOKEN ARM, UNDECLARED BUT LIVE: with max_bytes set and no max_tokens, token_ceiling() derives 59,168 / 2.27 = 26,065 tok and clamps it to the 25,000 read cap; config_defects() reports only a DECLARED max_tokens above the cap, so this clamp is silent. The verdict (about 20,193 tok, ok) is computed at the seed's 2.93 B/tok -- this is the one file on this config using that fallback; at the 2.27 floor the same bytes read 26,065, over. Left as is, deliberately: no max_tokens declared; re-judge after --calibrate.

THE CEILING IS THE READ CAP MINUS ITS SIBLING'S: 25,000 - 6,100 = 18,900 tokens, so the two per-file ceilings SUM to the read cap exactly (see classes.read-set; re-split from 19,200 in S20). bytes_per_token 2.8225 is MEASURED, 2026-09-17, on blob 4811f02 -- the file at 53,229 B after the action-ledger wording -- by the doubled-file method: the doubled read reports 37,717 tokens, so the file is 18,858.5. The same run reproduced 37,731 on blob 2a3e410d (53,252 B, after the PR #82 review-response edits), which gave the previous 2.8227 (S22). A DENSITY IS TIED TO THE BLOB IT WAS MEASURED ON: the previous value 2.8248 was measured on blob c0550acd (008d656, 52,195 B) and carried unchanged through two later edits of this file, so the tool reported 22 tokens of headroom where there were 2.5 (PR #82 review, section 3). Re-measure whenever `git rev-parse HEAD:starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md` no longer reads 4811f02; measured_bytes only warns at 25% drift, which is not a substitute. The tool counts int(53,229 / 2.8225) = 18,858, 42 under the ceiling: every future byte of this file is paid for by a reduction elsewhere in it (the PR's own rule) unless the partition is re-split.

16 TOKENS OF HEADROOM under the re-split 6,100 (S20; it was a no-growth pin at 5,800 after #80). bytes_per_token 2.8155 is MEASURED, 2026-09-17, on blob ed49b97 -- the file at 17,129 B after the five-file cap's row gained its `bin/sync` sentence -- by the same method (seven copies read as 42,586 tokens, so the file is 6,083.7). The same run reproduced 42,208 on blob 933816b4 (17,024 B, after the ratchet row gained its manifest-removal and merge/rebase sentences), which gave the previous 2.8234 (S22); left at 2.8234, the tool counted the new blob at 6,066, 18 tokens under its real size. The previous 2.8191 was measured on blob 656beae7 (main at 9fa3141, 16,353 B) and had gone stale by the same mechanism as the runner's, by one edit; benign here (6,038 reported vs 6,029.7 real) but the same rule applies: re-measure whenever `git rev-parse HEAD:starter-kit/SAFEGUARDS.md` no longer reads ed49b97. The tool counts int(17,129 / 2.8155) = 6,083. The pair, measured file by file, is 18,858.5 + 6,083.7 = 24,942.2 tokens, 99.77% of the cap (read together on 933816b4 and 2a3e410d it was 49,789 doubled = 24,894.5); the two ceilings still partition it exactly. PROPOSAL -- the split of the partition is a choice.

structure.why: the Learnings table's own row shape, which bin/check-learnings parses for contiguity. A shape check is cheap and two malformed rows once stood for ~40 sessions before anything looked.

files._: ON-DEMAND, so NO max_tokens by design: the read cap binds a file read WHOLE, and this file is read in PART -- measured over 80 transcripts on the fork, read whole once and in part 243 times, and a partial read returns whole ROWS. The unit actually paid is the row, and the primary guard is bin/check-learnings' ROW_BUDGET_BYTES = 1,500 B per row (canonical-only), whose two independent bases that checker restates in its own comment; this entry is the long-form home that comment points at. bytes_per_token 2.8897 was MEASURED 2026-08-29 on blob b21854cc -- the exact blob cea3068 carries (46 rows, 56,673 B) -- by the doubled-file method: `cat F F > x.md`, Read x.md with a spanning `limit`, halve the token count the refusal reports (an over-cap explicit limit returns no content and costs nothing). max_bytes 73,728 is a PROPOSAL, the fork's ceiling: derived on 2026-08-26 at the pre-compaction density 3.0300 as the size that stays inside one read even if every new byte is 20% denser. At today's 2.8897 it sits 1,486 B ABOVE the one-read cliff (25,000 x 2.8897 = 72,242 B), so read it as a growth signal, not a guarantee of one read; a re-derivation at today's density would land near 70,000 B. NO max_line_bytes: a per-row cap set anywhere useful is red on day one against rows nobody may edit.

_deliberate_exclusions: Measured on cea3068 and left out on purpose, with the numbers a future session needs: README.md 74,636 B, ITERATIVE_METHODOLOGY.md 55,976 B, FRAMEWORK_APPARATUS.md 15,493 B, HOW_TO_USE.md 55,528 B, starter-kit/BOOTSTRAP.md 28,211 B. Large, but read on demand and by humans (or by an adopter at setup), not mandated at Phase 0; the two the series shrank (ITERATIVE_METHODOLOGY.md via #78, its apparatus into FRAMEWORK_APPARATUS.md) now each fit one read, which is the argument, not their size. Adding any of these means declaring a ceiling nobody has defended yet, which is policy, not provisioning. THE TWO ROOT LEDGERS, removed from files[] by PR #80 review F3 (the entries are recoverable with `git show 37740763:.context-budget.json`): CHANGELOG.md (113,835 B on the merge into main at 9fa3141, about 46,135 tokens at its measured 2.4674 B/token) and HANDOFFS.md (101,162 B, about 42,778 tokens at 2.3648). Neither is read whole: both are newest-on-top, Phase 0 reconciles each against git log, and a session reads the newest entries and the one newest receipt, so a whole-file token verdict measures a read nobody makes. Declared in a whole-read class, a ledger past about 60 KB is over for good -- token_ceiling() clamps every whole-read file to the 25,000-token read cap whatever its max_bytes says -- and --precommit refused every append to either (measured: +300 B, refused); pinning max_bytes at the current size refuses the next append as well. What bounds them is methodology_trim.py's archive trigger (196,608 B for a root ledger; `python3 starter-kit/methodology_trim.py --check --file CHANGELOG.md --file HANDOFFS.md`), so each ledger now has one size limit, not two (review F4).
_synced: DELIBERATELY EMPTY. The seed ships two synced entries (SESSION_RUNNER.md, SAFEGUARDS.md) that drift-check an adopter's local copy against a canonical checkout. THIS REPO IS THAT CANONICAL: pointing path and canonical at the same file would compare a blob to itself, an identity no change can falsify. Here those two files are editable, so a SIZE finding is actionable -- which is why they carry per-file ceilings in files[] under read-set instead. check_synced() is drift-only and never enters an aggregate; a max_bytes written into a synced entry would look configured and refuse nothing.
